speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've had this lesion and if you have any history of diabetes or circulation problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Does the lesion have a raised, firm border, and have you noticed any joint pain or other skin changes recently? I would also like to check if the area is warm to the touch.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the history of an ant bite, the painful ulcer with purplish borders, and your history of Crohn's disease, this presentation is highly suggestive of pyoderma gangrenosum. I would like to rule out infection and vascular causes, so please allow me to examine the lesion closely and check for systemic signs.

REQUEST TEST: Wound_Culture_and_Sensitivity
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal lab results help rule out a systemic infection, which supports an inflammatory etiology like pyoderma gangrenosum given your Crohn's history. To further distinguish this from vascular ulcers or other conditions, have you experienced any recent changes in your bowel habits or gastrointestinal symptoms?

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_Lesion_Edge

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The biopsy confirming neutrophilic infiltration without infection, combined with your history of Crohn's disease and the classic presentation following minor trauma (pathergy), strongly supports the diagnosis. 

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
